headline: Medium risk: shared customer-support data and allowlisted egress create leakage and cascading-error pathways; prompt injection and compliance risks are lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not proven. However, agent_a uses CLI/session memory and agent_b is a LangChain4j framework that may consume upstream text; if outputs are manually bridged or copied, prompt-like content could influence B. Uncertainty keeps this above none.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are copied into agent_b prompts or files
IF a shared workspace or clipboard is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste bridging during review
Add a short prompt-prefix sanitizer before feeding A into B
Use a human review step for any text passed from A to B

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a explicitly touches personal data, finance data, support history, and documents, while agent_b has no documented data-class limits and no isolation controls. Because agent_a has allowlisted egress, sensitive content could leave the pair if B receives A's context or if either agent is pointed at shared data. The shared-data pathway is plausible in default support workflows.
conditions: IF both agents access the same support workspace or ticket corpus
IF agent_b is configured to ingest agent_a transcripts or files
mitigations: Restrict both agents to a redacted test dataset
Remove personal and finance fields before any handoff
Disable outbound calls for the session
Separate credentials and workspaces per agent

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can run multiple instances and has allowlisted network egress, while agent_b has no documented write or network capabilities. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable-resource writes, so conflict is limited. Uncertainty about hidden write surfaces in agent_b prevents none, but the blast radius appears small.
conditions: IF both agents are given write access to the same external resource
IF agent_b is wrapped with additional tools that add filesystem or API writes
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time
Assign separate API keys per agent
Use read-only mounts for shared inputs
Add a lock file or queue for any shared resource

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a is a memory/workflow system that can emit decisions and successful implementations, and agent_b is a general LLM framework that may render or act on upstream text. If B treats A's output as authoritative, errors can cascade into support workflows. No verification step is documented, so the default pathway is plausible.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a outputs without a verification step
IF downstream actions are triggered from B's rendered summaries
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before actioning outputs
Require citations or source links in A's output
Have B label A-derived content as untrusted
Limit B to summarization, not execution

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a touches personal data and finance data, but agent_b has no documented residency, retention, or certification controls. That mismatch creates a plausible compliance gap if the same regulated data flows through both. Because agent_b's compliance posture is undocumented, uncertainty escalates to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is routed through both agents
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the shared workflow
mitigations: Route only de-identified records through the pair
Document retention and deletion handling before deployment
Keep regulated data out of agent_b until controls are verified
Review vendor terms and data-processing agreements
